text: If the potential difference between the two ends of a metallic wire is doubled, the drift speed of free electrons in the wire:
explanation: v_d = eEτ/m and E = V/l. Doubling V doubles E, so the drift speed doubles.

text: A metre bridge is balanced with a known resistance R in the left gap and an unknown resistance S in the right gap. The balance point is at l cm from the left end. When the battery and the galvanometer are interchanged, the balance point will:
options: shift left or right depending on the values of R and S
explanation: The balance condition R/S = l/(100 − l) is unchanged when the battery and galvanometer are interchanged (reciprocity of the Wheatstone bridge), so the balance point stays the same.

text: Lorentz force in vector form is:
explanation: The magnetic (Lorentz) force on a charge q moving with velocity v in field B is F = q(v × B). The order of the cross product matters: B × v gives the opposite direction.

text:
Assertion: When an electric current is passed through a moving coil galvanometer, its coil gets deflected.
Reason: A circular coil produces a uniform magnetic field around itself when an electric current is passed through it.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Assertion is false and Reason is true
explanation: The coil deflects because of the torque on a current loop in the radial field of the permanent magnet, so the Assertion is true. The field produced by a circular coil is not uniform around it, so the Reason is false.

text: When a ray of white light is incident obliquely on the first surface of a prism, then:
explanation: Refractive index is highest for violet light (shortest wavelength), so violet is deviated the most and red the least.

text: The de Broglie wavelength (λ) associated with a moving electron having kinetic energy E is given by:
explanation: λ = h/p and p = √(2mE), so λ = h/√(2mE).

text: The majority charge carriers in a P-type semiconductor are:
explanation: P-type semiconductors are doped with trivalent impurities, which create holes; holes are the majority carriers.

text: Four resistors form a bridge between terminals P (top) and Q (bottom): upper-left arm 10 Ω, upper-right arm 10 Ω, lower-left arm 25 Ω and lower-right arm X. A 5 Ω resistor joins the left and right corners. When a battery is connected across P and Q, no current flows through the 5 Ω resistor. The value of X is:
explanation: No current in the 5 Ω resistor means the Wheatstone bridge is balanced: 10/25 = 10/X ⇒ X = 25 Ω.

text: The relative permeability of substance X is slightly less than one and that of substance Y is slightly more than one. Then:
options: X is paramagnetic and Y is ferromagnetic
X is diamagnetic and Y is ferromagnetic
X is paramagnetic and Y is diamagnetic
X is diamagnetic and Y is paramagnetic
explanation: μr slightly < 1 ⇒ diamagnetic; μr slightly > 1 ⇒ paramagnetic. (Ferromagnetic materials have μr ≫ 1.)

text: If the kinetic energy of moving electrons is made four times, their de Broglie wavelength becomes:
explanation: λ = h/√(2mE) ∝ 1/√E. Making E four times makes λ half.

text: Two long parallel wires MN and ST are each part of a separate circuit: MN with battery E₁ and resistor R₁, ST with battery E₂ and resistor R₂. A student wanted the wires to repel, but they attract each other. What change should the student make so that they repel?
options: Reverse the terminals of both batteries E₁ and E₂
Reverse the terminals of battery E₁ or E₂
Choose supply voltages such that E₁ = E₂
Add a key and an ammeter to the circuit
explanation: Parallel wires attract when their currents are in the same direction and repel when opposite. Reversing one battery reverses the current in one wire only; reversing both keeps them attracting.

text: An N-type semiconductor is one which has:
options: a majority of holes as charge carriers
a majority of free electrons as charge carriers
a trivalent element added as an impurity
an equal number of holes and free electrons
explanation: N-type is doped with a pentavalent impurity, so free electrons are the majority carriers.

text:
Assertion: When a convex lens made of glass is completely immersed in water, its focal length increases.
Reason: The refractive index of glass with respect to water is greater than that of glass with respect to air.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: 1/f = (μ_rel − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). In water μ_rel = 1.5/1.33 ≈ 1.13, smaller than 1.5 in air, so f increases (Assertion true). The Reason is false: glass's refractive index relative to water is less than relative to air.

text:
Assertion: Diffraction of light is difficult to observe in everyday situations but can be observed in laboratory conditions.
Reason: To produce diffraction of waves, the size of an obstacle must be comparable to the wavelength of the waves.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: Light has a very small wavelength (~10⁻⁷ m); everyday obstacles are far larger, so diffraction is negligible. In the lab we use very narrow slits comparable to λ, so diffraction becomes visible. The Reason explains the Assertion.

text: An electric eel can generate a voltage of up to 800 V. If it can supply a current of 5 mA, the maximum power it can deliver is:
A collimated beam of protons travels with constant velocity along the X-axis. A current-carrying solenoid also has its axis along the X-axis. If the beam enters the solenoid along its axis, it will:
explanation: Inside the solenoid B is along its axis, parallel to the protons' velocity. F = q(v × B) = 0 when v ∥ B, so the beam is undeflected.

text: An electron, a proton, a deuteron and an alpha particle are all accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Which one has the maximum de Broglie wavelength?
explanation: λ = h/√(2mqV). For the same V, the particle with the smallest product mq has the longest wavelength — the electron.

text: The magnetic susceptibility of a material is found to decrease with a rise in its temperature. The material is:
explanation: By Curie's law, the susceptibility of a paramagnetic material is inversely proportional to absolute temperature (χ ∝ 1/T). Diamagnetic susceptibility is practically independent of temperature.

text: When a p-n junction diode is forward-biased:
options: it acts as an insulator and no current flows through it
it offers a low resistance and a large current flows through it
it offers a high resistance and a small current flows through it
the width of the depletion region increases
explanation: Forward bias lowers the potential barrier and narrows the depletion region, so the diode offers low resistance and a large current flows.

text: When a biconvex lens of glass of refractive index 1.6 was dipped in a certain transparent liquid, it behaved like a plane sheet of glass. The refractive index of the liquid is:
explanation: The lens has no power when the relative refractive index is 1, i.e. when the liquid has the same refractive index as the glass: 1.6. Light then passes undeviated.

text:
Assertion: In Young's double slit experiment, the first bright band for blue light is closer to the centre than the first bright band for green light.
Reason: Blue light has a longer wavelength than green light.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Assertion is false and Reason is true
explanation: y₁ = λD/d ∝ λ. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than green, so its first bright band is closer to the centre (Assertion true). The Reason is false — blue has the shorter wavelength.
